profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record near Rush, New York, a small town in the Rochester metropolitan area in Monroe County, is tagged as a data center under the name Landmax Data Systems. Landmax Data Systems is a real company, but its business is property records, not IT hosting: it collects local property assessment data, tax map coverage and comparable sales information for New York municipalities, and sells access to that information through web based and desktop research tools used by assessors, appraisers and title researchers. Reverse geocoding the stored coordinates places the address on East Henrietta Road in the town of Rush with no business name attached in the underlying map data, consistent with a small office rather than a large facility. Nothing about Landmax's public description, a records and data services company serving the New York property and municipal assessment market, matches the profile of a commercial or enterprise data center that leases server space, power or network connectivity to outside tenants. The telecom data center classification on this OpenStreetMap record appears to be a mistag, most likely applied because the company's name contains the words Data Systems, rather than a description of what actually operates at this address. No capacity or infrastructure figures are offered because the site does not appear to be a data center in the sense this registry otherwise documents.

reading.body:
This record tags an address in Rush, New York as a data center operated by Landmax Data Systems, but research confirms Landmax is a property assessment and municipal records company that sells tax maps and comparable sales data to assessors and appraisers. The company's name contains "Data Systems" but describes no IT hosting business, and reverse geocoding the coordinates shows a small office on East Henrietta Road with no data center infrastructure apparent. The telecom data center classification appears to be a mistag rather than a description of actual operations.

No capacity or infrastructure specifications are published for this site because it does not operate as a commercial data center leasing power, space, or connectivity to outside tenants. Research has been exhausted and the entry is unresolvable as a facility relevant to AI infrastructure.

This record should not be counted among New York's mapped data center capacity and does not affect assessment of the state's ability to support AI scaling.
